name: Basophils (absolute count)
rangeNote: Basophils are the rarest white cells, so such small counts are hard to measure exactly; analysers sometimes count other cells as basophils. There is no meaningful lower limit.
summary: Basophils are the rarest white blood cells. They release histamine and take part in allergic reactions. This value is how many are in a set volume of blood.

high.meaning: A slightly high count can be a counting error or linked to allergies or inflammation, and a repeat test may be normal. A count that stays high is worth discussing with a doctor, because some blood disorders raise it.
commonCauses: Counting error by the analyser (a false high)
Blood disorders such as chronic myeloid leukaemia (rare)

low.meaning: A low or zero count is common and usually means nothing, because so few basophils circulate.
